title: review check answer
description: One judgement per finding the review's hunter raised: real or not real, and the one line of code evidence that decided it. The driver drops only a finding judged not real; a finding with no judgement is kept, and an answer it cannot read keeps them all.

skills.description: Every skill invoked in this step: none, so always empty. The driver cross-checks it against the Skill calls in the run log.

judgements.description: One per listed finding, by its id.

id.description: The finding's id, exactly as listed.

real.description: The verdict, given first: true when the defect the finding describes is in the code as it stands; false only on evidence that it is not.

reason.description: After the verdict, one line quoting the exact code, with its line number, that shows the finding is real or not real.

rule.description: Last, the one rule the claim breaks, from this list, so the same mistake counts as one thing across changes whatever its wording: failure-shown-as-success: a failed read, write or step reads as success, as empty, or as nothing; wrong-source-of-truth: a value read, counted, dated or credited from the wrong place; one-path-of-several: a rule or change applied on one path, screen or caller, and missing on the others; race-or-unlocked-write: two things at once collide: a read-then-write with no lock, a stale answer landing late; screen-out-of-step: what the screen shows disagrees with the saved state: a stale label, a wrong undo, an early success; dead-or-unwired: a control or behaviour that does nothing, or was never connected; ticket-part-missing: something the ticket or plan asked for is not in the change; access-or-privacy: data or an action reaches someone it should not; data-lost-or-stranded: data dropped, overwritten, or left where a later step or a deletion cannot reach it; edge-case-unhandled: a boundary not handled: a timezone, a page break, an empty list, a retry, old saved data; test-proves-nothing: a test that cannot fail, or that checks the wording of a file and not the behaviour; docs-out-of-step: a doc, prompt or comment that says something the code no longer does; reimplements-existing: hand-writes what a helper or kit part already does; off-design-kit: a raw colour, size or layout outside the kit; overflow, wrapping or spacing slips; unbounded-cost: slow or costly as it grows: unbounded reads, a query per row, a call that repeats; other: none of these.
